bug_semantics: GuardDog's ZIP extraction path in safe_extract() (originally PackageScanner.download_compressed) unpacked wheels/eggs/zips with zipfile.ZipFile.extract() over namelist() and never inspected ZipInfo.file_size, member count, or compressed-to-uncompressed ratio. TAR archives went through tarsafe, but ZIP had no analog, so a tiny malicious PyPI/npm package could expand to gigabytes of disk and deny scanning/CI. CWE-409 zip-bomb DoS; GHSA/CVE affected < 2.7.1, patched in 2.7.1.
flaw_origin: ZIP support was added so PyPI .zip packages could be scanned. The first write (PR #105 member cd08be9) appended an elif zippath.endswith('.zip') branch that extracted every member with no size, ratio, or file-count guard. A later same-PR refactor moved that exact loop into guarddog/utils/archives.py::safe_extract(); later formatting and a path-join cleanup (61ddd72) did not add bomb limits. Limits appear only in b2e10d2.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-22870/GHSA-ffj4-jq7m-9g6v is a published CWE-409 zip-bomb in GuardDog ZIP extraction. Before ZIP support, download_compressed only extracted .tar.gz via tarsafe and refused other suffixes. cd08be9 added ZIP extract of every namelist entry with no decompressed-size, ratio, or file-count validation, which is the flawed mechanism. 9337a82 is a same-PR move of that loop into safe_extract(); 72fe2db is the GitHub squash of PR #105 onto main (tree-identical to 9337a82) and is therefore not the BIC. Parent 37c7d07 was checked directly: product code has no zip.extract/safe_extract. Mainline -L/-S confirm the unguarded extract persists through v2.7.0; 61ddd72 only drops the extra os.path.join path (a distinct path-traversal issue) and still extracts without bomb limits. The first commit that closes this CWE-409 sink is b2e10d2, which inspects ZIP infolist sizes and raises via _check_compression_bomb; that commit is in v2.7.1 and not v2.7.0, matching the advisory range. GHSA's referenced c3fb07b is a same-day helper refactor on top of that fix, not the introduction of the limits. AI-second: the BIC commit object is a human Datadog engineer with no AI/co-author/bot marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than FALSE_POSITIVE (the advisory is real and still published).
